description: Passionate university students interested in space, AI, robotics, and technology. We’re looking for creative and motivated teammates skilled in AI/ML, data science, programming, engineering, astronomy, or design. Let’s build an innovative solution together!
summary:
Trend Detective is a scientific web platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, focusing on flash droughts—sudden droughts that devastate crops within weeks before traditional alerts trigger.

Using live NASA POWER API data (root-zone soil moisture), our FastAPI-powered platform:

Detects flash droughts via a rigorous, published scientific definition (Ford & Labosier, 2017).

Analyzes historical trends using Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope tests.

Screens risk with a 0-100 index for rapid regional triage.

Forecasts risk 7, 14, and 30 days ahead using an explainable LightGBM AI model (validated by 119 automated tests).

Built with HTML/JS and a Python backend, the site is highly transparent. We explicitly label the 30-day forecast as experimental, flag a known 2016 NASA data anomaly, and state clearly that this is a statistical early-warning system, not a weather forecast.

The modular engine can be extended to other phenomena like heat waves, transforming raw NASA data into actionable climate intelligence for farmers, insurers, and NGOs.
details: **Trend Detective** is an interactive Earth science web platform built with **Python (FastAPI)**, **HTML5/CSS3/Vanilla JavaScript**, **Leaflet**, and **Chart.js** that turns **NASA POWER** satellite data (1981–present) into instant, statistically verified climate diagnostics for any location on Earth. By clicking anywhere on the interactive map, users trigger a multi-variable scan across 12 climate indicators using dual trend testing (**OLS linear regression** with Student’s $t$-test and non-parametric **Mann–Kendall / Theil–Sen slope**) alongside a transparent 0–100 phenomenon risk score, filtering out noise to highlight only statistically significant changes. Beyond long-term trends, the platform integrates **three calibrated LightGBM machine learning models** (using FAO-56 evapotranspiration, water balance, and local 2005–2014 daily baselines) with **SHAP** explainability to forecast the probability—and meteorological drivers—of a **flash drought** starting within the next **7, 14, or 30 days**, giving researchers, planners, and communities fast, zero-setup, and actionable climate intelligence.
